_comment: AstroDoc AI countermeasure cards (SPEC §7.4). topic = what the card treats; hazard = NASA HRP hazard. demoProtocol=true means the steps are team-authored placeholders that the cited document supports only in general terms, so the UI must show a 'demo protocol' tag.

cards.title: Reduce radiation exposure time
steps: Limit time spent in low-shielding modules until readings return to your mission average.
Log your dosimeter reading every 2 hours.
Report the trend to the crew medical officer at the next daily conference.

cards.title: Increase shielding around rest areas
steps: Move your sleep station to the most shielded area of the habitat.
Use water containers and stowage bags as extra shielding walls around the sleep station.

cards.title: Antioxidant-rich food and hydration
steps: Keep to antioxidant-rich menu items (fruit, vegetables) in the mission nutrition plan.
Maintain hydration per the mission nutrition plan.

cards.title: Solar particle event: go to the storm shelter now
steps: Go to the designated storm shelter immediately.
Stay in the shelter until mission control or the commander gives the all-clear.

cards.title: Solar particle event: crew headcount and dose tracking
steps: Commander performs a crew headcount in the shelter.
Every crew member records a dosimeter reading every 30 minutes.
Postpone all EVAs until the event is over.

cards.title: Protect the next sleep window
steps: Protect your next scheduled sleep window; no tasks scheduled inside it.
Follow the lighting schedule: bright light on waking, dim light 1 hour before sleep.
Ask the commander to reduce your workload today.

cards.title: Caffeine timing
steps: No caffeine within 6 hours of your sleep window.

cards.title: Severe sleep loss: stand down from critical tasks
steps: Do not perform EVA, robotics or other safety-critical tasks until rested.
Take a protected sleep period as soon as possible.
Notify the crew medical officer.

cards.title: Rest and re-measure heart rate / blood pressure
steps: Stop strenuous activity and rest for 10 minutes.
Re-measure heart rate and blood pressure sitting, then lying down.
Drink fluids per the mission hydration plan.

cards.title: Possible cardiovascular distress: stop and notify the crew medical officer
steps: Stop all activity now and lie down or anchor yourself in a resting position.
Notify the crew medical officer immediately.
Re-measure heart rate, blood pressure and SpO2 every 5 minutes until the CMO arrives.

cards.title: Keep up the exercise countermeasure program
steps: Continue the prescribed daily aerobic and resistance exercise once readings are back in range.
Do not skip exercise sessions; they counter cardiovascular and muscle deconditioning.

cards.title: Cabin CO2 above normal: ventilate and check the scrubber
steps: Check the CO2 reading for your module and the CO2 scrubber status.
Increase ventilation or move to a well-ventilated module; CO2 can collect where air does not circulate.
NASA's limit is a 1-hour average of 3 mmHg (NASA-STD-3001): report readings that stay above it.
Watch for headache, fatigue or shortness of breath - early signs of CO2 exposure - and report them.

cards.title: High cabin CO2: leave the module and alert the crew
steps: Move to a module with normal CO2 readings now.
Alert the crew and mission control; follow the onboard atmosphere contingency procedure.
Check SpO2 and report headache, dizziness or shortness of breath to the crew medical officer.

cards.title: Low SpO2: rest, re-measure, check cabin air
steps: Rest and re-measure SpO2 after 5 minutes, with the sensor positioned correctly.
Check the cabin CO2 and O2 readings for your module.
If CO2 is elevated, move to a well-ventilated module and report it.

cards.title: Very low SpO2: notify CMO, oxygen protocol
steps: Notify the crew medical officer now.
Follow the onboard oxygen protocol in the medical checklist.
Check cabin atmosphere readings and alert the crew if they are abnormal.

cards.title: Correct blood glucose with the nutrition plan
steps: If glucose is low: take a fast-acting carbohydrate from the mission nutrition plan.
If glucose is high: skip extra snacks and drink water.
Re-measure blood glucose in 15 minutes.

cards.title: Critical blood glucose: notify CMO
steps: If low and you can swallow safely, take fast-acting carbohydrate now.
Notify the crew medical officer.
Re-measure in 15 minutes.

cards.title: Fever: re-measure, hydrate, isolate shared items
steps: Re-measure body temperature in 30 minutes.
Drink fluids per the mission hydration plan.
Avoid sharing items (cups, towels, headsets) with crewmates.
Notify the crew medical officer.

cards.title: High fever or hypothermia: CMO now
steps: Notify the crew medical officer now.
Medication only per the onboard medical checklist or flight surgeon.
Re-measure temperature every 15 minutes.

cards.title: Low mood: connect and recover
steps: Optional: book a private conference with the ground psychologist.
Make contact with a crewmate today (shared meal, short talk).
Schedule a recovery activity you enjoy in the next 24 hours.

cards.title: Persistent very low mood: involve the CMO
steps: Talk with the crew medical officer today.
Book a private conference with the ground psychologist.
Stay with crewmates; avoid working alone today.

cards.title: Emergency symptom: first actions
steps: Stop what you are doing and stay still in a safe position.
Call a crewmate to you now; do not stay alone.
The crew medical officer follows the onboard emergency medical checklist.
Medication only per the onboard medical checklist or flight surgeon.
